findings.summary: Lag and rolling features are computed over the whole frame without grouping by store_id or sorting by date, so later stores' first rows take lags from the previous store and unsorted input yields wrong lags.

FEATURES now requires past sales, so build_features on a future-dated frame without sales yields all-NaN lag columns that dropna empties; even with history appended, sales_lag1 and sales_mean7 are only valid one day ahead (risk, not confirmed).

test_calendar_features passes only by coincidence after the first 7 rows are dropped (2026-01-08 is also a Thursday in January), and the new lag test uses a single store so nothing covers the multi-store lag bug.
